channel.description: Latest articles from BK Reader (The Brooklyn Reader) (bkreader.com)

item.title: Eastern Brooklyn to Get First 2-K Seats This Fall
item.description: Families who live in School Districts 18 and 23, which covers Canarsie, Remsen Village, Brownsville and Ocean Hill, can apply for a free, 2-K seat that will be available in the 2026-2027 school year.

item.title: The Growing Interest in Online Entertainment Across Local Communities
item.description: In a world where sidewalk cafés and neighborhood parks have long been the heart and soul of our communities, a fresh kind of gathering spot is popping up—one that doesn’t need a subway ride or a reservation.

item.title: MTA Bus Driver Accused of Punching Midwood 16-year-old
item.description: An MTA bus driver was arrested after allegedly punching a 16-year-old during an argument near Bay Parkway, leaving the teen hospitalized with possible facial injuries.

item.title: NYPD Cadet Indicted for Alleged Rape of a Teen Girl in Flatbush
item.description: Ahmed Elnahtawy, 24, was arraigned Tuesday and charged with rape, sexual abuse, forcible touching and sexual misconduct. He is accused of assaulting the teen at her home in Flatbush.

item.title: Listen, Sketch, Move: March at The Brooklyn Museum
item.description: You can listen to the Brooklyn Symphony Orchestra, write poetry and learn how to protect the sea.

item.title: Here’s What New Yorkers Complained About Most in 2025
item.description: High retail prices, online scams and auto issues topped New Yorkers’ complaints in 2025, according to the Office of New York Attorney General Letitia James.

item.title: Thousands of Empty NYCHA Apartments Pose Security Risk
item.description: Vacant NYCHA apartments rose to 6,740 in May 2025 from approximately 2,840 in January 2022. Some of the vacant apartments, without adequate security measures, create opportunities for illegal occupancy by unauthorized individuals, some of whom use the apartments as a base for illegal activities, city investigators found.

item.title: Half of NYC's Top Speeders Drive in Brooklyn
item.description: The top speeder, who drives often in southern Brooklyn, has been caught speeding by school zone speed cameras more than 1,000 times since mid-2023, according to new data from Transportation Alternatives and Families For Safe Streets.

item.title: 2026 Spark Prize Honors Brooklyn’s Equity Champions
item.description: At Brooklyn Org’s Spark Breakfast at Barclays Center, five organizations were celebrated for their dedication and service to the borough.
